reproduction_target: An entirely in-silico structure-function mapping study of the cardiac sarcomere. The computational target is: (1) obtain 3D protein models for MYH7 (subfragment 1, residues 1-840), MYBPC3, TNNT2, TNNI3, MYL2 and MYL3 by four modelling routes - pre-computed AlphaFold Protein Structure Database models (AlphaFold Monomer v2.0 pipeline, database snapshot 2022-11-01), ColabFold v1.5.5 on AlphaFold2 v2.2 weights with MMseqs2 homology search (with and without user-supplied PDB templates, run on Stanford's Sherlock GPU cluster), and AlphaFold 3 via the hosted AlphaFold Server; (2) select the best model per gene using mean pLDDT, mean PAE and minimal RMSE against named experimental cryo-EM/crystal structures (PDB 8ACT, 8EFH, 8EFI, 8ENC, 8G4L, 6CXJ, 6G2T, 7LRG, 7TIJ, 5TBY, 6KN7, 6KN8, 7UTI, 7UTL), with alignment and visualisation in PyMol 2.5.8; (3) assemble a variant table combining the Sarcomeric Human Cardiomyopathy Registry (SHaRe; 12,326 HCM patients, 4,427 with variants in the six genes, 1,056 unique variants), UK Biobank exomes (346,977 individuals with variants in the genes of interest, 1,479 unique variants), gnomAD v4 (730,947 exomes; 4,620 unique variants) and 77,482 AlphaMissense pathogenicity scores, with a deduplication plus 50%-expansion selective-inclusion rule that adds the highest-scoring predictions to the disease set and the lowest-scoring to the population set; (4) run a binomial spatial scan statistic over the 3D models with sliding spheres of radius 10, 15 and 20 Angstrom, computing a per-residue log-likelihood ratio and assessing significance by a 1,000-permutation label-shuffling test; (5) validate the enriched regions against ClinVar (accessed through ClinVar Miner, data current to 2024-02-05; 5,252 annotations) with Fisher's exact test, against age of disease onset in SHaRe with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test and Kaplan-Meier curves, and against an unnamed independent HCM cohort reported only in the supporting materials. No wet-lab step is reported: the study generates no new experimental data and performs no new structure determination.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v2 JATS source XML. WebFetch returned HTTP 403; the same .source.xml was retrieved cleanly by curl with a browser user-agent (200, 149,687 bytes) and was confirmed to be the correct paper by an exact match on the title string 'Spatial genomics of the cardiac sarcomere'. 14 computational steps, 0 wet-lab steps. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE FINDING: the article contains NO Data Availability section, NO Code Availability section and NO software-availability statement of any kind. A full URL sweep of the JATS XML returns only the CC-BY-NC-ND licence URL, an ORCID URL and XML namespace URIs - there is no GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo, figshare, OSF or Code Ocean link anywhere in the manuscript, and no GEO/SRA/ENA/ArrayExpress/dbGaP/EGA accession. The bioRxiv v2 landing page was also fetched (200, 147,764 bytes) and likewise contains no repository or data-availability statement. Per the collection protocol no web search for an unstated repository was performed: absence of a repository is recorded as the finding. Consequently the code axis is scored from prose describability alone. The four named public/general-purpose tools (AlphaFold DB, ColabFold, the AlphaFold Server, PyMol) are third-party software that a re-implementer can obtain, but not one line of this study's own analysis code - the variant-set assembly, the AlphaMissense selective-inclusion rule, the binomial spatial scan implementation, the permutation test, and all statistics and figures - is deposited or linked, so code=0 on every step that carries the study's own logic. Version scoring rule applied: a prose pin counts (version=1) only when the paper text itself gives at least major.minor. Qualifying pins: ColabFold v1.5.5, AlphaFold2 v2.2 model weights, AlphaFold Monomer v2.0 pipeline with the 2022-11-01 database snapshot, PyMol 2.5.8, and the dated ClinVar Miner extraction (2024-02-05). Non-qualifying: 'AlphaFold 3' / 'the AlphaFold Server' (a hosted service with no version and no snapshot date), gnomAD 'v4' (major only - v4.0 and v4.1 differ), MMseqs2 (no version, and the UniRef and environmental database releases are unnamed), AlphaMissense (no release or file version), the UK Biobank exome release (200k/450k/500k not stated), the SHaRe data freeze date, and every statistical procedure (Fisher's exact, Wilcoxon rank-sum, Kaplan-Meier, the spatial scan itself) which is named as a method with no software, language or library behind it. An internal inconsistency is also recorded: Methods states ColabFold v1.5.5, while Results repeatedly compares against 'ColabFold v2.3 with templates' - a version string that does not correspond to any ColabFold release and is unreconciled in the text. Nothing was executed and no code was read (none exists to read).

steps.label: Retrieval of pre-computed monomer models for the six sarcomeric proteins from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, stated verbatim as generated by 'the AlphaFold Monomer v2.0 pipeline and last updated on November 1, 2022'. The pipeline version and the database snapshot date are both given, which is the strongest version evidence in the paper; UniProt accessions are not listed, so the entries must be re-identified from the gene symbols, and no download script, date-of-access or checksum is recorded

Structure prediction with ColabFold v1.5.5 on AlphaFold2 v2.2 model weights using MMseqs2 homology search, run on Stanford's Sherlock GPU cluster, in custom-template mode with the per-gene PDB templates listed in Methods (MYH7: 8ACT, 8EFH, 8EFI, 8ENC, 8G4L; MYBPC3: 6CXJ, 6G2T, 7LRG, 7TIJ, 8G4L; MYL2/MYL3: 5TBY, 8ACT, 8G4L; TNNT2/TNNI3: 6KN7, 6KN8, 7UTI, 7UTL). Run settings are unusually well recorded for prose - recycles=3, early stopping tolerance auto, relax limited to 200 iterations, greedy pairing strategy, dropout disabled, MMseqs2 browsing UniRef and environmental datasets - but no random seed is given, MMseqs2 carries no version, the UniRef and environmental database releases are unnamed and undated, the number of models/ensembles is not stated, and no invocation script or config is deposited

Structure prediction with AlphaFold 3 through the hosted AlphaFold Server, used for 'all protein-ion and protein-ligand interactions'. The server is a closed, credential-gated Google DeepMind web service with usage limits and terms of use; no server version, no model snapshot date, no seed, no ion or ligand specification (which ions, which ligands, at what stoichiometry), no job configuration and no output PDB/CIF deposit are given, and no local re-execution path exists because AF3 weights are not freely redistributable

Model quality assessment by computing mean pLDDT and mean PAE per predicted model across the four modelling routes, used to rank models per gene (reported values include MYH7 pLDDT 73.75 / PAE 23.43 A, MYBPC3 79.38 / 25.43, MYL2 83.36 / 13.21, MYL3 88.86 / 11.14). No software, script, language or library is named for the aggregation; no residue range, masking rule or chain selection is stated for the PAE mean even though the paper itself notes that S2 and LMM regions dominate the error for MYH7; and the predicted model files (ColabFold and AlphaFold Server outputs) are not deposited, so only the AlphaFold-DB subset of the inputs is publicly retrievable

Structural superposition of each predicted model onto the named experimental PDB structures and measurement of the 'minimal root mean square error (RMSE)', with visualisations and alignments made using PyMol 2.5.8 (reported values include MYH7 1.35/3.73/3.71/6.39/3.25 A, average 3.67 A; MYL3 1.48 A vs 8ACT and 1.12 A vs 5TBY). PyMol 2.5.8 is an exact pin but is commercial/licence-gated. No alignment command is given (align vs super vs cealign), no outlier-rejection cycle count or cutoff, no chain or residue-range selection, no definition of what 'minimal' RMSE minimises over, and no .pml script is deposited - so the reported RMSE values cannot be regenerated deterministically from the prose

Extraction of HCM disease-observed variants from the Sarcomeric Human Cardiomyopathy Registry (SHaRe): 12,326 HCM patients of >17,000 registry patients, 4,427 with variants in the six genes, 1,056 unique variants. SHaRe is a consortium registry to which access is possible only through a collaboration/data-access request; the paper gives no accession, no registry URL, no data-access-committee or application route, no data freeze or extraction date, and no variant QC/transcript/nomenclature convention (which RefSeq or Ensembl transcript defines the residue numbering that the spatial scan then uses). No extraction query or script is deposited

Extraction of population reference variants from UK Biobank exome data, stated as 346,977 individuals carrying variants in the genes of interest yielding 1,479 unique variants 'without applying and filtering based on MAF'. UK Biobank is legitimate controlled access, but the paper names no UKBB application/project ID, no exome release (the 200k, 450k and ~500k releases give materially different denominators and the stated 346,977 matches none of them on its face), no field IDs, no variant-calling pipeline (GATK vs DRAGEN callsets differ), no genome build, and no QC filter set. No extraction code is deposited

Extraction of population reference variants from gnomAD, stated as 'its latest release (v4)' with 730,947 exomes of which 416,555 originate from the UK Biobank, giving 586,403 individuals with variants in the six genes and 4,620 unique variants, again without MAF filtering. gnomAD data are fully public, but 'v4' is a major-version-only citation (v4.0 and v4.1 differ in variant QC and in the frequency tables), no access date is given, no genome build or canonical-transcript choice is stated, and the overlap between gnomAD and the separately counted UK Biobank set is not deduplicated in any stated way even though the paper itself notes the 416,555 overlap. No query, VCF filter expression or extraction script is deposited

Retrieval of ClinVar clinical significance annotations for the six genes through the ClinVar Miner tool, 'with data current up to February 5, 2024', giving 5,252 annotations of which 945 pathogenic/likely pathogenic and 1,391 benign/likely benign, with variants having multiple or discordant submissions counted as separate annotations. The snapshot date is a genuine pin and the source is public, but no ClinVar Miner tool version or query URL is recorded, no review-status (star-rating) filter is stated, no assertion-criteria or submitter filter is stated, and the resulting annotation table is not deposited

Integration of AlphaMissense pathogenicity predictions (77,482 scores across the six genes, all 19 possible missense substitutions per position) into the discrete disease/population framework: deduplication against the SHaRe and population sets, ranking by predicted pathogenicity, then expansion by the stated rules AddedDiseaseVariants = sorted Predictions[0:N_Disease x 0.5] and AddedPopulationVariants = sorted Predictions[N_Population x 0.5 : N_Population], described as increasing the analysed variant count by 50% while holding the disease:reference ratio constant. The formulas are given but the AlphaMissense release/file version is not, the transcript and isoform used for the score lookup is not, the sort direction and tie-breaking rule are not, and the second formula's index range as written is internally ambiguous. The classification is a study-specific procedure with no deposited implementation

The core analysis: a binomial spatial scan statistic over the selected 3D models, sliding spheres of radius 10, 15 and 20 Angstrom centred iteratively on every amino acid, computing p_in, p_out and the overall rate r and the binomial log-likelihood ratio per window, with significance from a permutation test of 1,000 permutations in which variant labels are shuffled with the per-residue variant count held constant. The statistical definitions are written out, but this is a study-specific implementation with NO code deposited anywhere, no language or library named, no random seed for the 1,000 permutations, no stated multiple-testing correction across the three radii, six genes and all residue centres, no rule for which atom (CA, centroid, any atom) defines residue position or how multi-chain/multi-copy models are handled, and no significance threshold stated in Methods. Its inputs also inherit the controlled-access SHaRe and UK Biobank sets

ClinVar validation of the identified enriched regions: qualitative inspection of histograms of pathogenic and benign variant distributions inside versus outside the regions, and a quantitative comparison of pathogenic/likely-pathogenic against benign/likely-benign proportions using Fisher's exact test. No statistical software, language, package or version is named, the test is not specified as one- or two-sided, no multiple-testing handling across the tested regions is stated, and no analysis script or contingency table is deposited

Disease-onset phenotype analysis comparing age of disease onset for SHaRe patients carrying variants inside the enriched spheres against those outside, assessed with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test and Kaplan-Meier curves. No statistical software or version is named, 'age of disease onset' is not operationally defined (age at diagnosis vs age at first symptom vs age at first SHaRe encounter), the censoring rule and time origin for the Kaplan-Meier curves are not stated, no covariate adjustment or handling of related/duplicate carriers is described, and the underlying patient-level data are the controlled-access SHaRe registry with no access route given

External validation on 'an independent dataset containing variant information of patients diagnosed with HCM', with the results stated to be presented in the supporting materials. The cohort is not named anywhere in the main text, has no accession, no institution, no size, no access route, no ethics/consent statement and no described analysis; the supporting information is listed in the JATS only as an opaque 'DC1' item. Nothing about this step is recoverable from the manuscript

headline.static_readiness: 0/14 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI on 2 of 14 computational steps (14%), NI on 10, X on 2. The readiness upper bound is 2/14 = 14%, and the binding constraint is not version discipline but the total absence of any deposited analysis code. This paper has NO code availability statement, NO code repository of any kind, and NO data accession; a full URL sweep of the JATS XML yields only the licence URL, an ORCID and XML namespace URIs. Every step that carries the study's own logic - variant-set assembly from three cohorts, the AlphaMissense 50%-expansion selective-inclusion rule, the binomial spatial scan implementation with its 10/15/20 A spheres, the 1,000-permutation significance test, Fisher's exact validation, and the Wilcoxon/Kaplan-Meier onset analysis - scores code=0. The two RI steps (C1, C2) are precisely the two steps that lean on third-party software the authors did not write: retrieval of AlphaFold DB models (AlphaFold Monomer v2.0 pipeline, snapshot 2022-11-01) and ColabFold v1.5.5 on AlphaFold2 v2.2 weights, whose run settings are recorded in unusual prose detail (recycles 3, early-stop auto, relax 200 iterations, greedy pairing, dropout disabled, custom templates by PDB ID). Two steps are X rather than NI: C3 runs AlphaFold 3 through the closed, credential-gated AlphaFold Server with no version, no seed and no ligand/ion specification, so there is no re-execution path at all (proprietary ceiling); and C14, the external validation cohort, is an unnamed dataset with no size, no institution and no access route, described only as living in the supporting materials. Data access is the second structural constraint: two of the three variant cohorts are controlled (SHaRe, a consortium registry with no stated access route or freeze date; UK Biobank, with no application/project ID, no exome release and no callset named), so even a re-implementer with perfect code could not assemble the same input table. Version evidence is real but partial and unevenly distributed: five exact pins exist (ColabFold v1.5.5, AlphaFold2 v2.2 weights, AlphaFold Monomer v2.0 with a dated snapshot, PyMol 2.5.8, ClinVar 2024-02-05) while the AlphaFold Server, MMseqs2 and its UniRef/environmental databases, AlphaMissense, the UKBB release, the SHaRe freeze and every statistical procedure carry no version at all - hence capture_claim = exact_pins_partial with no lockfile, container or environment file claimed anywhere. A specific internal inconsistency should be put to the authors: Methods pins ColabFold v1.5.5, but Results repeatedly evaluates 'ColabFold v2.3 with templates', a version string with no corresponding ColabFold release. Stage-2 upside is nil by construction - there is no repository to verify - which is why stage2_candidate is false; this paper reaches Stage 2 only if the orchestrator draws it in the stratified audit.
headline.coverage: 14 computational analysis steps assessed from the bioRxiv v2 JATS 'Materials and Methods' and its subsections (Development of protein models / Computational modelling approach; Protein template selection; Assessment and comparison of predicted protein structures; Datasets - SHaRe, UK Biobank, gnomAD, AlphaMissense, ClinVar; Classification of variants; Integration of pathogenicity prediction model; Spatial Scan Statistic; Validation Strategies - ClinVar validation, Disease onset age analysis, External validation set). 0 wet-lab steps: the study generates no new experimental data, performs no new structure determination, and re-uses existing registries, biobanks, prediction databases and deposited PDB structures throughout. Coverage = 14/14 (100%) of enumerated steps; computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 14/14 = 100%.

gaps.where: All 14 computational steps; fatally for C10 (AlphaMissense selective inclusion), C11 (binomial spatial scan and permutation test), C12 (Fisher's exact validation) and C13 (Wilcoxon / Kaplan-Meier onset analysis)
gaps.missing: The manuscript contains no Code Availability statement and no repository link of any kind. A complete URL sweep of the bioRxiv v2 JATS source XML returns only the CC-BY-NC-ND licence URL, one ORCID URL and XML namespace URIs; the v2 landing page likewise carries no repository reference. The entire analytical apparatus of the paper - cohort assembly and deduplication across SHaRe, UK Biobank and gnomAD, the AlphaMissense 50%-expansion rule, the 3D binomial spatial scan implementation, the 1,000-permutation significance machinery, and all figure-generating statistics - exists only as prose description.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the analysis code (cohort assembly, AlphaMissense integration, spatial scan, permutation test, validation statistics, figure scripts) in a public repository, archive a tagged release to Zenodo for a citable DOI, and add a Code Availability statement naming that DOI and the commit used for the published figures.

gaps.where: C11 (binomial spatial scan statistic), C10 (variant classification), C6/C7/C8/C9 (cohort extraction)
gaps.missing: The spatial scan is the paper's central methodological contribution and is described only by its statistical formulas. Undetermined from prose: which atom defines a residue's position for the sphere test (CA, side-chain centroid, any-atom minimum distance), how sphere centres step across the structure, how multi-chain or multi-copy models and disordered/low-pLDDT regions are handled, whether the three radii are analysed jointly or separately, what multiple-testing correction is applied across residues, radii and six genes, what significance threshold defines an 'enriched region', and how contiguous significant spheres are merged into the reported regions. No random seed is given for the 1,000 label permutations.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the spatial-scan implementation with its configuration, state the residue-position convention, the sphere-centre stepping rule, the multiple-testing correction and the significance threshold explicitly in Methods, and fix and report the permutation seed.

gaps.where: C3 (AlphaFold 3 predictions via the AlphaFold Server), C5 (PyMol 2.5.8)
gaps.missing: AlphaFold 3 is used exclusively through the hosted AlphaFold Server, a credential-gated Google DeepMind service with usage limits and terms of use, whose model weights are not freely redistributable. No server version, model snapshot date, seed, job configuration, or ion/ligand specification is given, and the resulting structures are not deposited - so this step has no re-execution path even in principle. PyMol 2.5.8 is a commercial Schrodinger product (licence-gated); it is exactly pinned, which is the mitigating factor, but its use is still a paid-licence dependency.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the AlphaFold Server output structures (mmCIF/PDB) with their job specifications, seeds and the ion/ligand composition for every prediction, so that the downstream evaluation is checkable even where the prediction itself cannot be re-run; and provide an open-source alternative path (or at minimum a deposited .pml script) for the PyMol alignment and visualisation.

gaps.where: C3 (AlphaFold Server / AlphaFold 3), C2 (MMseqs2), C4 (pLDDT/PAE aggregation), C10 (AlphaMissense), C11/C12/C13 (all statistical procedures), and the whole analysis environment
gaps.missing: No environment capture of any kind is claimed: no container, no image digest, no conda environment file, no lockfile, no requirements file, no interpreter version, no operating system, no package channel. Beyond the environment, entire tool versions are absent: the AlphaFold Server / AlphaFold 3 has no version and no snapshot date, MMseqs2 has no version, AlphaMissense has no release or file version, and every statistical procedure (Fisher's exact, Wilcoxon rank-sum, Kaplan-Meier, the binomial spatial scan) is named as a method with no software, language, package or version behind it. The only exact prose pins are ColabFold v1.5.5, AlphaFold2 v2.2 weights, AlphaFold Monomer v2.0 with a dated database snapshot, PyMol 2.5.8 and the ClinVar 2024-02-05 extraction - hence capture_claim = exact_pins_partial. A separate defect: Methods pins ColabFold v1.5.5 while Results repeatedly evaluates 'ColabFold v2.3 with templates', a version string that matches no ColabFold release and is never reconciled.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a software table giving an exact version for every tool including MMseqs2, AlphaMissense, the AlphaFold Server access date and the statistical environment (language, version, and every package version); ship a solved lockfile or a container referenced by digest; and correct or explain the ColabFold v1.5.5 versus v2.3 discrepancy between Methods and Results.

gaps.where: C6/C7/C8/C9/C10 (variant table assembly), C11 (spatial scan inputs), C13 (onset analysis)
gaps.missing: The variant-to-residue mapping that the entire spatial analysis operates on is never deposited and never fully specified. No transcript or isoform is named for any of the six genes, so the residue numbering that defines every sphere is unanchored (MYBPC3 and MYH7 in particular have isoform-dependent numbering); no genome build is stated; no HGVS nomenclature convention is given; and the assembled table of 1,056 SHaRe, 1,479 UK Biobank and 4,620 gnomAD unique variants with their disease/population/excluded labels is not provided as a machine-readable supplementary file. The overlap between gnomAD v4 and the separately counted UK Biobank exomes (the paper itself states 416,555 of 730,947 gnomAD exomes come from UKBB) has no stated deduplication rule at the individual level.

Not pinned: the MMseqs2 UniRef and 'environmental' database releases used to build every ColabFold MSA (unnamed and undated, and these determine the predictions that everything downstream rests on); gnomAD cited as 'v4' with no minor version and no access date, where v4.0 and v4.1 differ; AlphaMissense with no release or file version; and the PDB template/comparison structures cited by ID with no download date (PDB entries can be versioned and re-refined). No checksums or persistent DOIs are given for any downloaded resource.

gaps.missing: Every stochastic component of the study is unseeded in prose. ColabFold/AlphaFold2 predictions depend on a random seed and on MSA subsampling; the AlphaFold Server likewise; and the 1,000-permutation label-shuffling test that supplies all reported significance has no stated seed and no stated random number generator. None of the predicted structures or the permutation null distributions are deposited, so not even a distributional comparison is possible against the published values.
